newsitem.title: SPAIN: Small Spanish companies not ready for euro - BBV.
newsitem.headline: Small Spanish companies not ready for euro - BBV.

text.p: Small- and medium-sized Spanish companies need to make an effort to adapt before the new European single currency arrives, a top official at Banco Bilbao Vizcaya said on Friday.
"Spanish companies are not mentally prepared for the launch of the euro," executive vice president Pedro Luis Uriarte told a conference on the euro.
According to a BBV survey of small- and medium-sized companies, only 11.8 percent of those polled are taking measures to prepare for the euro.
BBV's study showed that in general labour-intensive businesses will bear the greatest burden from the euro launch, while capital-intensive businesses should not suffer as much.

The study showed that just over half of those surveyed expect the single currency to benefit the Spanish economy, while 29.8 percent said it would have no effect and 12.2 percent said it would be negative.
